candidates.prompt_text: What healthy routine do you do every day? Please describe it and say when you usually do it.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names one healthy daily routine and states the usual time or part of the day when they do it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear routine; simple description of the action; a time reference such as morning, after school, or before bed; understandable pronunciation of common everyday words.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any simple personal example is acceptable, such as drinking water in the morning, walking after school, stretching before class, or sleeping early.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about another person’s routine, discussing unhealthy habits only, giving general facts about health without a personal routine, or describing a special event instead of a daily habit.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For pronunciation, listen for clear vowel and consonant sounds in common words, understandable word stress, and whether the response can be followed easily without frequent repetition.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Listing several activities without describing one, forgetting to mention when the routine happens, speaking too softly or too fast, or pronouncing key words unclearly.

candidates.prompt_text: Tell me about a healthy food or drink you often have. When do you usually have it?

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker mentions one healthy food or drink they often have and says when they usually have it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Name of one food or drink; a simple description such as taste, temperature, or why they choose it; a time reference like breakfast, lunch, after exercise, or evening; clear pronunciation of familiar food words.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any common healthy choice is acceptable, for example water, fruit, soup, vegetables, or yogurt, as long as the speaker connects it to their own routine.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Describing cooking steps in detail, talking about expensive diets, comparing many foods without answering the time question, or discussing nutrition science.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Focus on intelligibility: can a listener understand the main words the first time? Notice word endings, stress in two-syllable words, and smooth production of short phrases.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Naming many foods but not choosing one, not saying when they have it, using memorized lists, or unclear pronunciation of simple food and time words.

candidates.prompt_text: Do you do any simple exercise to stay healthy? Describe it and say where you usually do it.

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker says whether they do a simple exercise, describes the activity, and gives the usual place where they do it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: One clear exercise activity; a brief description of what they do; a place such as at home, in the yard, at school, or in a park; understandable pronunciation of action words.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any accessible activity is acceptable, including walking, stretching, running, skipping, or simple exercises in a room or open space.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about watching sports, discussing professional training, describing a team match instead of a personal routine, or giving medical advice.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Assess whether the student pronounces common exercise words clearly enough to be understood, with reasonable rhythm and pausing in short sentences.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Answering only yes or no, forgetting to mention the place, giving an unrelated story, or unclear pronunciation of the main activity word.
